sections.heading: Egyptian numerals and additive representation
paragraphs: Additive Egyptian-style notation counts repeated landmark symbols. A symbol can stand for one, ten, a hundred or another power of ten; their contributions add. formulas.meaning: Even+even and odd+odd are even; even+odd is odd. A product with an even factor is even. Two odd factors multiply to an odd result because (2p+1)(2q+1)=2(2pq+p+q)+1. Checking examples helps find a rule but does not prove it for every integer.
formulas.restriction: The controls use nonnegative integers; parity rules extend to all integers.

misconceptions.mistake: A collection of examples proves a parity rule.
misconceptions.correction: Use algebra to cover arbitrary integers; use a counterexample to disprove an overly broad claim.
